about: Every LLM log store on this Mac: where it lives, who writes it, who reads it, who cleans it and by what criterion. Measured daily by `bin/system-doctor logstores`, cleaned by `bin/log-sweep` (cleaner `sweep`, any kind). Registering a store is adding an entry here; writers are never constrained. kind: log = written by a tool on its own and accumulating, counted in the doctor's total, growth and top list; app = app data, binaries, profiles or outputs, listed so the fallback skips it, never measured or counted. readers (log only): the programs that read it (grep of llm-legs, token-map, review-bench, claude-setup, usage-ai-report), plus the vendor CLI where it reads its own store back (resume, rewind); [] fires the doctor's `log-unread`. cleaner: self = the writer prunes it, sweep = bin/log-sweep, cap = the app caps it, keep = never deleted, measured only. Criterion (at most one): days (a unit untouched that long: a file by its mtime, a directory by the newest mtime inside it), max_mb (the newest units within that many MB), keep_newest (that many newest units), tail_mb (a file truncated to its last N MB). One glob match is one unit; "type": "file" keeps only regular files this user owns, "type": "dir" only directories this user owns; a socket, FIFO or device is never a unit, and a unit some process holds open is never swept.

stores.name: tmp-sandboxes
stores.writer: agents, workers and suites (probes, mutation and replay sandboxes)
readers: the agent that made it, while live
stores.why: top-level sandboxes left behind (listenprobe, segprobe, j128, crit-a1, suite temp dirs); a week idle, a dir held open is skipped. $TMPDIR only by mktemp/tempfile and our own prefixes: macOS services keep their dirs there too; a new prefix reaches the fallback at 200 MB
